signals.title: Ask HN: Should we shut down current AI strategy? Vent Your Heart Out
signals.summary: I don't know, maybe it's just me. Does it feel to you like we're boiling the oceans in a desperate attempt to build something "smarter than human?" Do you notice that the idea that "AI will cure cancer" is predicated on the belief that we've found the data that will lead to a cure and us humans just somehow missed it? Are you also watching your former boss, who laid you off for AI, slowly turn the nail gun that is AI automation towards his own face? Are you also currently avoiding plane flights at all costs? Personally, I like AI a lot, but I think conversational language models were a mistake. Isn't this the root of AI psychosis for most? Isn't autocomplete turned conversational just sycophancy for our delusions even if we have guardrails in place? Don't you think that if you can't explain the functionality of an AI model that means you probably shouldn't use it? If you said yes to any of the above I'd love to hear your thoughts on the current state of things. Please, vent your heart out. If you said no to everything please just be quiet, this will be fun for the rest of us. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50542654 Points: 3 # Comments: 4

signals.title: SLED: Sensor SLicing from Edge to Datacenter
signals.summary: arXiv:2611.21937v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern sensing systems generate large volumes of heterogeneous data streams from multiple sensor modalities, increasing reliance on datacenters for computation, artificial intelligence/superintelligence (AI/SI) inference, and AI/SI training. Each sensor stream may have different network and compute requirements depending on its type and data volume. However, current wireless systems typically allocate resources at the device level, leading to contention among co-located sensor streams, where bulk data transfers may starve latency-critical telemetry. To this end, this paper introduces Sensor Slicing (SL). SL provides deterministic, medium access control (MAC)-level isolation for individual sensors within a single user equipment (UE) in open radio access networks (O-RAN). Using agentic coding techniques, SL is implemented in two O-RAN-compliant packages, reducing development time by 400 times (2 h 40 min [OCUDU] vs. 6.5 weeks [OAI]), 228-fold fewer human prompts (4 vs. 913), and less than half the tokens (0.64B vs. 1.43B). signals.title: WebAgents: Unbundling Agent Creation, Hosting, and Execution for an Agent-Native Web
signals.summary: arXiv:2611.21978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are moving from isolated assistants toward autonomous agents that can plan, use tools, and coordinate with others, motivating an emerging Agentic Web of independently developed agents and services. Realizing this vision requires agent behavior to move across creators, hosts, and runtimes without coupling publication to a particular execution environment or transferring authority over user resources. We introduce WebAgents, which unbundles these roles through a signed agent.pkg that carries portable workflows, skills, schemas, and resource requirements. An OpenClaw-based agent-native browser/runtime verifies the package, obtains authorization, and binds it at run time to user-controlled models, tools, permissions, and budgets, while hosts distribute the public program and may retain private services server-side. We demonstrate this contract with three unrelated workflows executed unchanged under local and API-backed models, including literature review with live services and a website-published travel agent using semantic tools and user-selected personal resources.
